New technologies — adaptive learning platforms, virtual tutoring, large language models — are entering schools faster than the evidence base can keep up. My dissertation builds the evidence two ways. The first chapter is a program evaluation: it asks whether a hybrid tutoring intervention works, and for whom, developing a causal-inference strategy that generalizes a regression discontinuity estimate from the eligibility cutoff to the full population a program serves. The second chapter is a measurement study: it asks when scores produced by LLM classifiers are reliable enough to support inferences about people, developing a generalizability-theory framework for AI-based measurement systems. Together the chapters cover the two questions any organization deploying new technology must answer — does it work, and can we trust how we measure it.
